about: Literature reference values for validation tests and presets (issue #15). Human-readable companion: references.md. Read that file's 'Status' section first: no paper full text could be fetched for this version, so 'verified' is empty and every candidate is under 'wanted'. No number in this file comes from memory.

verified.id: short slug, also the preset name
verified.slot: one of: single_beam_tweezer | counter_propagating_or_standing_wave | linear_paul | ring_paul | hybrid_paul_optical | parabolic_mirror
verified.setup: a Setup file (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4); must pass levtrap.setup.parse unless schema_gaps is non-empty
verified.schema_gaps: list of setup keys that the current schema does not support yet, written as ARCHITECTURE.md section 4 says the future schema will (e.g. focus.kind = 'parabolic_mirror')
verified.provenance: map from setup key path to {value, source, flag}; flag is 'stated' or 'inferred'; source names page/section/figure/table
verified.expected: list of {quantity, value, unit, source, tolerance_rel, why}
verified.agreement_note: what agreement to expect and why

wanted.citation: as above; metadata_source says where the bibliographic data came from
wanted.skeleton: field kinds and geometry only (no numbers), as they would appear in the Setup
wanted.schema_support: 'current' if the current Setup schema can express the trap, else 'future' with schema_gaps
wanted.needed: parameters to read from the paper
wanted.expected_quantities: measured quantities to read from the paper
wanted.agreement_note: what agreement to expect once the numbers are in, and why

citation.authors: V. Jain, J. Gieseler, C. Moritz, C. Dellago, R. Quidant, L. Novotny
citation.title: Direct Measurement of Photon Recoil from a Levitated Nanoparticle
citation.metadata_source: web-search index (APS accepted-manuscript link, alphaxiv listing); not checked against the paper

wanted.trap_type: single focused beam through a high-NA lens, silica nanosphere, ultrahigh vacuum, feedback cooled
needed: trapping power at the focus (and whether it is before or after the objective)
objective NA and whether the back aperture is overfilled (filling factor)
particle radius or diameter and how it was measured
expected_quantities: trap frequencies along x, y, z
recoil heating rate vs power and vs radius
gas damping rate vs pressure, if given
wanted.agreement_note: The effective NA of an overfilled or apodised objective is rarely stated, and levtrap's lens model assumes an ideal aplanatic focus; expect the frequency ratios to agree better than the absolute frequencies, which may be off by tens of percent. The recoil heating rate scales with scattered power, so once the frequencies are matched it should agree to the paper's stated uncertainty plus the radius uncertainty (rate ~ r^6).

citation.title: Thermal broadening of the power spectra of laser-trapped particles in vacuum
citation.journal: J. Phys. B: At. Mol. Opt. Phys. 50, 245501 (2017)
citation.metadata_source: web-search index (arXiv listing metadata); not checked against the paper

wanted.trap_type: retro-reflected beam forming an optical lattice (standing wave), silica particle, vacuum (geometry to be confirmed from the text)
needed: power in each pass and the retro-reflection loss
focusing NA or waist of each pass and the relative focus positions
expected_quantities: trap frequencies along x, y, z
wanted.agreement_note: The axial frequency of a standing wave is set by the fringe contrast, i.e. by how well the returning beam overlaps the incoming one; this is seldom stated, so expect the axial frequency to tens of percent and the radial frequencies (set mostly by the waist and power) to be closer. Model as two coherent beams with opposite directions.

citation.authors: L. Dania, D. S. Bykov, F. Goschin, M. Teller, A. Kassid, T. E. Northup
citation.title: Ultrahigh Quality Factor of a Levitated Nanomechanical Oscillator
citation.metadata_source: web-search index (arXiv DOI page, journal news items); not checked against the paper

wanted.trap_type: linear Paul trap, charged silica nanoparticle, room temperature, extreme high vacuum
needed: geometry (efficiency) factors, or the electrode drawing to compute them
particle radius and charge (number of elementary charges)
expected_quantities: Mathieu q and a, if given
dissipation rate and quality factor vs pressure
wanted.agreement_note: Secular frequencies depend on q/m and on geometry factors that only an electrode simulation gives; if the paper states the measured charge and the geometry factors, the Mathieu secular frequency should agree to a few percent, otherwise only the scaling with RF voltage can be tested. The measured damping at the lowest pressures is below the gas-damping model's reach and should be compared only where gas damping dominates.

citation.authors: J. Millen, P. Z. G. Fonseca, T. Mavrogordatos, T. S. Monteiro, P. F. Barker
citation.title: Cavity Cooling a Single Charged Levitated Nanosphere
citation.metadata_source: web-search index (UCL repository copy, arXiv listing under preprint title 'Cavity cooling a single charged nanoparticle'); not checked against the paper

wanted.trap_type: Paul trap inside a single-mode optical cavity (hybrid electro-optical), charged silica nanosphere. Electrode geometry (ring or otherwise) NOT confirmed: must be read from the paper before this fills the ring-trap slot.
wanted.schema_support: current for the Paul part; the cavity field is out of scope
schema_gaps: optical cavity field (not planned in ARCHITECTURE.md)
needed: RF amplitude and frequency, DC voltages
cavity parameters only if the cavity-free secular frequencies are not reported separately
expected_quantities: secular frequencies with the cavity field off
wanted.agreement_note: Only the Paul-trap secular frequencies are comparable; the cavity cooling itself is outside levtrap. If a better-documented ring or wheel trap paper is found, it should replace this entry for the ring_paul slot.

citation.authors: G. P. Conangla, R. A. Rica, R. Quidant
citation.title: Extending vacuum trapping to absorbing objects with hybrid Paul-optical traps
citation.metadata_source: web-search index (arXiv PDF listing, publisher indexing); not checked against the paper

wanted.trap_type: weak tightly focused beam overlaid on a Paul trap, giving a dimple in the Paul pseudopotential
needed: Paul trap geometry, RF amplitude and frequency, DC voltages
expected_quantities: secular frequencies with Paul trap only, optical trap only, and combined
any reported depth or stability boundary
wanted.agreement_note: The hybrid sum is a direct test of levtrap's 'sum the fields' design. Expect the combined frequency to follow the summed stiffness to the accuracy of each part separately; the absolute numbers inherit the NA uncertainty of the optical part and the geometry-factor uncertainty of the Paul part.

citation.authors: E. Bonvin, L. Devaud, M. Rossi, A. Militaru, L. Dania, D. S. Bykov, M. Teller, T. E. Northup, L. Novotny, M. Frimmer
citation.title: Hybrid Paul-optical trap with large optical access for levitated optomechanics
citation.metadata_source: web-search index (arXiv listing, DOAJ record); not checked against the paper

wanted.trap_type: Paul trap combined with a high-NA optical tweezer; particle held by optical, RF, or combined fields
expected_quantities: secular frequencies in the Paul trap alone
wanted.agreement_note: Second hybrid entry, useful because the abstract (as indexed) says the particle can be held by optical fields, RF fields or both, so each field can be checked separately before the sum.

citation.authors: J. Vovrosh et al. (full author list to be read from the paper)
citation.title: Parametric feedback cooling of levitated optomechanics in a parabolic mirror trap
citation.metadata_source: web-search index (arXiv PDF listing, Optica abstract URI josab-34-7-1421); only the first author was given; DOI not found in the index (the Optica URI suggests 10.1364/JOSAB.34.001421, unconfirmed)

wanted.trap_type: single beam focused by a parabolic mirror, silica nanoparticle, feedback cooled in 3D
schema_gaps: trap.fields[0].focus.kind = 'parabolic_mirror' (ARCHITECTURE.md section 4 lists it as a later focus kind; milestone E)
needed: mirror focal length and aperture (or effective NA)
expected_quantities: trap frequencies along x, y, z
wanted.agreement_note: A parabolic mirror focuses with an apodisation unlike an aplanatic lens and with a large solid angle; until a parabolic-mirror focus exists, any lens stand-in should be expected to miss the frequencies by tens of percent. This entry is for milestone E.
